newsitem.title: GERMANY: Siemens cuts 6,000 German jobs in 1995/96.
newsitem.headline: Siemens cuts 6,000 German jobs in 1995/96.

text.p: German electronics and engineering group Siemens AG cut about 6,000 domestic jobs in the business year ended September 30, personnel director Werne Maly said.
The company showed a net rise in its worldwide workforce, however, as the domestic job cuts were more than offset by increases in jobs in other countries, he said.
As of September 30, 1995, Siemens had 381,000 employees worldwide, 211,000 of them in Germany.
Maly said the thousands of Siemens workers who participated in work stoppages protesting job cuts on Monday would not be paid for their time off the job.
Siemens does not plan to resort to further legal measures as it does not wish to hinder the coming wage negotiations, but it may be forced to if it suffers heavy damages from the lost work-hours.
Siemens is trying to reduce its costs for Christmas and vacation payments, which now total over one billion marks a year. It will try to reduce its sick pay costs by cutting vacation time, he said.
